Instructions: the spec's gcc/<name>.c files compiled with clang -march=rv32imc_xgap9 -O2 give the same mnemonic multiset as GAP9 GCC's .s files. The only difference is that GCC loads a folded constant with lui+lw from the constant pool, where clang uses a single lui. One case is equivalent but differs: f32abs of a union-bitcast integer is selected as p.bclr rd,rs,0,31 instead of fabs.s. A DAG combine turns fabs(bitcast) into an integer AND, which clears the same bit, so the result is identical. No libcalls appear at O0/O2/O3/Os in my kernel.

Semantics on GVSoC. My own test (logs/20-F036-review/gvsoc/) has 1566 unary inputs: 66 special values (both zeros, infinities, qNaN/sNaN with payloads, denormals, +-2^31 and its neighbours, halves, +-3e9) plus 1500 random values, including 600 multiples of 0.25. It also has 5856 max/min pairs (66x66 special values plus 1500 random), loop forms for max, min, clamp, the rounding sum and sqrt(abs), and 24 constant-argument cases. The reference is a host C model written from the RISC-V F spec (ref.c). GAP9 GCC and clang each ran at O0/O2/O3/Os on ri5ky_testbench via benchmarks/gap9-sweep/sim/run_sim.sh. Clang at all four levels matches the host reference except 148 lines. All 148 come from the GVSoC rmm defect below: a model of the reference that includes that defect (ref_gv.c) matches clang O0/O2/O3/Os and GCC O0 on every line.

Worker claim 1 CONFIRMED: GAP9 GCC constant-folds f32max/f32min with C MAX/MIN semantics, which contradicts its own run-time fmax.s/fmin.s. GCC -O2/-O3/-Os give max(NaN,1)=NaN, max(1,NaN)=NaN, max(-0,+0)=-0, min(-0,+0)=+0 and min(NaN,-inf)=NaN. GCC -O0 (which runs the instruction) gives 1.0, 1.0, +0, -0 and -inf, like the reference. So do all clang levels, whose DAG folding follows maximumNumber/minimumNumber. Clang agrees with the instruction semantics here; GCC's folding is the defect.

Worker claim 2 CONFIRMED: GVSoC's fcvt.w.s with rm=rmm returns 0x80000001 instead of 0x80000000 for every input <= -2^31, including exactly -2^31 (0xcf000000) and -inf. rdn and rup saturate correctly. The cause is in gvsoc2/core/models/cpu/iss/include/isa_lib/int.h:1956, lib_flexfloat_cvt_w_ff_round: it negates, adds 0.5, saturates to INT_MAX, then negates. GCC and clang hit it identically. Every other rounding and saturation case matches the spec: NaN gives 0x7fffffff, values >= 2^31 give INT_MAX, halves round away from zero for rmm, and rdn(-0.5)=-1, rup(-0.5)=0.

Feature gating. Clang accepts all 7 builtins with rv32imc_xgap9, rv32imc_zfinx_xpulpv2 and rv32imfc_xpulpv2 (ilp32 and ilp32f), and also with zdinx/zhinx + xpulpv2, which imply Zfinx. It rejects them with 'needs target feature xpulpv,(f|zfinx)' for rv32imc_xpulpv2, rv32imfc, rv32imc_zfinx and rv32imc. GAP9 GCC accepts them only under -march=...xgap9, with or without f. Tested with -Werror=implicit-function-declaration, because without it GCC silently treats an unknown builtin as an implicit external call. GCC rejects them for rv32imfcxpulpv2, xpulpv3 and xgap8. By contrast, its sibling builtins (dotsp2, CoreCount) are accepted under xpulpv2 and gap8. So clang is a harmless superset: the fork gates all its GAP9 builtins on xpulpv (159 records), the task asked for xgap9/zfinx+xpulpv/f+xpulpv, and outside GAP9 the builtins still emit standard F/Zfinx instructions.
